items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Speaking of Dizzy, I was working with Benny Carter at the Three Deuces, and he needed a trumpet player and I recommended Dizzy.

ctx.x: otherwise. And as I say he was -- I always admired him because he was -- you had to put him over there. He was different. But any way, let me take a breather. Okay? [pause in tape]

Are we back? Good. Speaking of Dizzy, I was working with Benny Carter at the Three Deuces, and he needed a trumpet player and I recommended Dizzy. I don't think Benny was really aware of Dizzy, but any way he hired Dizzy and the band was just tremendous. How I started working with Benny, at -- I think it was Kelly's Stables. I had been working, as I told you, with Fletcher Henderson, and man, we had been on the road, I'd been to Tupelo below Mississippi to two above Mississippi, two aside Mississippi. I was just…

And I went to New York, and Nat Cole -- I hadn't seen Nat in years because when I went to New York he went to California so I didn't see him, but I had heard about what he was doing. But any way this was -- now, this had to be in 1941, around 1941, so at the Kelly's Stables Nat Cole was appearing, and also Benny Carter's band. So I went in and I heard Nat's group, and it was just beautiful. I just loved it, you know, and it -- I was also glad to see him, and surprised to hear him sing, you know, because Nat and I…
